clue.text: Settle for a change in Oslo and nice

indicators.note: the letters of the two place-related words are made different, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone decides to move house, swapping Oslo for Nice on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges OSLO and NICE together; 'in' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a territory is to establish a colony there, populating it with incomers.

clue.text: Landlord's possible demand for stretcher hire

parts.note: a rack is the torture device that stretches its victim
to rent something is to hire it

explanation.surface: A request to hire an ambulance stretcher, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: A rack-rent is an extortionately high rent, the kind a grasping landlord might demand.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive, exploitative rent is something a greedy property owner could ask of tenants.

clue.text: Late deliveries expected

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
something due is expected to arrive

explanation.surface: Parcels that were expected have not turned up yet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowler's balls are called deliveries, and six of them make an OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something past its scheduled time is tardy, behind time.

clue.text: Muggy day clinched the sale

parts.note: muggy weather is close, humid and airless

explanation.surface: On a sticky, humid day a salesperson finally seals the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To close a sale is the sales idiom for completing a deal with a buyer.

clue.text: Bacon is more adventurous

definitions.meaning: comparative of rash, meaning more reckless or daring

explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a slice of bacon; rash means reckless, so the comparative form is bolder still.

clue.text: Val, gill and Abel go abroad — it's a small world!

indicators.note: going abroad means wandering about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Three travellers named Val, Gill and Abel head overseas and marvel at how small the world is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges VAL, GILL and ABEL GO; 'and' is just a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Marshall McLuhan describes a world shrunk by communications into one community.

clue.text: All out attack under officer…?

indicators.note: in a down clue the attack word is written below the officer word

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
to strike is to attack

explanation.surface: An all-out assault launched beneath a commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places STRIKE beneath GENERAL in this down entry. 'All out' is the union call for everyone to stop work.
explanation.definitionFit: When workers across every industry are called out together, the stoppage is a nationwide walkout.

clue.text: …dire prospects for renewing morale

indicators.note: renewing makes something over afresh, so these letters are remade in another order

explanation.surface: Grim prospects call for a boost to everyone's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewing' rearranges DIRE PROSPECTS; 'for' is a link word. The ellipsis ties it to the previous clue's strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the shared spirit and pride of a group, its collective morale.

clue.text: The forces of peace close to release

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces
to lock is to close or fasten

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops are near to freeing hostages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' reads as 'near' in the surface, but it is the verb meaning fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something held fast, you open its lock.

clue.text: The fruits of ramblers rambling so perish

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so these letters stray into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Hikers who wander about may come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramblers' looks like hikers, but rambling roses are climbing plants that bear these.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling roses are climbing plants, and their red seed pods are the fruit they produce.

clue.text: Friends without flippers left

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the flipper letters are taken away from the word friends

parts.note: fins are flippers, as on a seal or a swimmer's feet

explanation.surface: Seals or divers without their flippers have been abandoned by their mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes F, I, N and S, scattered through FRIENDS, leaving RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically, a red is someone on the left wing, a socialist or communist.

clue.text: Talking of liquid concoctions that injure

indicators.note: talking means the word for drinks is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: brews are drinks that are mixed or steeped

explanation.surface: A conversation about potions that cause harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bruise is to hurt by a blow that discolours the skin.

clue.text: Support the German in a French fix

parts.note: un is the French word for a
der is the German for the
to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A German man helps a Frenchman in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' reads as a predicament in the surface but is the verb meaning fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin is to prop up from below, giving a foundation.

clue.text: I have gone inside

indicators.note: the letters run across the inside of the words have and gone

explanation.surface: Someone announces that they have gone indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the 'I' in psychology.

clue.text: Customers' legal right to appear in court second

definitions.note: the possessive is a surface touch; the definition is the plural noun

indicators.note: the legal right term shows up inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Shoppers have a legal right to come into court next.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients are people who buy professional services, so patrons or buyers.

clue.text: Born in penury, for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: penury is poverty, or need

explanation.surface: A biographer notes someone was born into poverty, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims the final D from NEED; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a woman's maiden name, this French word means originally called, from birth.

clue.text: A very old cheese and dill ordered for starters — then fruit

indicators.note: starters are the first courses, so the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A menu offers vintage cheese and dill as appetisers, followed by fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is botanically a fruit, a large berry with one seed.

clue.text: Mixed a gin very sour

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are combined in another order

explanation.surface: A gin cocktail mixed badly tastes very sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasting acidic, like spoiled wine, is sharp and tart.

clue.text: 6.51 in Paris, for example, is politeness itself

indicators.note: the Roman numerals sit inside the word for a large town

parts.note: Paris is an example of a city
6 is VI and 51 is LI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: At 6.51 in Paris, as an instance, good manners are displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: '6.51' looks like a time but is two Roman numerals, VI and LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Civility is courteous behaviour, good manners.

clue.text: The cost of letters after a time

parts.note: post- is a prefix meaning after
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The price of mail rises after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee charged for sending mail.

clue.text: Highly impressive footwear

parts.note: shoes with very high, thin heels that leave dents, or impressions, in a soft floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'impressive' seems to mean admirable, but these sharp heels literally make impressions in floors.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilettos are women's shoes with tall, narrow heels, notorious for marking floors.

clue.text: Take off for a meal outside

indicators.note: the meal word goes around the outside of the letter a

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone leaves work to go out for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' as a phrase means leave, but here it is a rocket's lift-off; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a lift-off, as of a rocket or plane.

clue.text: Digital coverage that's inferior

parts.note: a cover for a digit, the toe, which sits low down; inferior in its anatomical sense of below

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital coverage' suggests online news, but a toe is a digit; 'inferior' means lower down, as in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced front of a shoe or boot covering the toes.

clue.text: Lack of grip shown by beginner?

parts.note: no means none, an absence or lack of
a vice is a tool that grips work firmly

explanation.surface: A newcomer struggles to get a firm hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grip' looks like a hold, but it is the workshop tool that clamps things.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a learner, someone new to an activity.

clue.text: Certain to lose right to prosecute

indicators.note: losing the letter means it is taken out of the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A lawyer is sure to lose the right to bring a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take legal action against someone.

clue.text: New live turn is very catching

indicators.note: new means made over in fresh form, so these letters take another order

explanation.surface: A fresh live act proves extremely popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LIVE and TURN; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A virulent disease is highly infectious, spreading readily.

clue.text: Aluminium found in blood, in abundance

indicators.note: the metal symbol is discovered sitting inside the blood word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Aluminium is detected in a blood sample in large amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in plenty, aplenty.

clue.text: Conversion factors tumble, hence extra gas

indicators.note: to tumble is to fall in a jumble, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Prices fall, so there is more gas to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: These rates are the multipliers used to convert one currency into another.
